newsitem.title: USA: Intel falls, fears arise on new chip flaw.
newsitem.headline: Intel falls, fears arise on new chip flaw.

text.p: Shares of computer chip maker Intel Corp fell nearly two percent Tuesday after reports about a possible flaw with the company's high-end Pentium chips.
Intel, based in Santa Clara, Calif., said it was looking into reports the Pentium II and Pentium Pro chips could contain a bug that causes the chips to make computational errors in some rare cases.
The problem was disclosed on Monday by Robert Collins, a Silicon Valley engineer who maintains a web site called Intel Secrets.

Earlier, Rodman and Renshaw cut its rating on Intel to neutral from buy and cut its earnings estimate for 1997 to $8.75 a share from $9.25. The firm also trimmed 1998 estimates to $10 a share from $11.

"Assuming these reports are correct, we expect that Intel will take very aggressive steps to correct the flaw," Rodman said in a research report. "These steps will likely include replacing approximately seven million Pentium Pro processors already shipped, for an estimated cost of $2.1 billion or about $1.50 per share."
